[0] Earlier this month, OpenAI, together with Astra, launched its first GPT-6 model. The GPT-6 series officially debuts two brand-new models—GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna—further expanding the product lineup.

[1] GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are available starting today

[2] According to the ChatGPT desktop app's update log, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna consume fewer tokens compared to their corresponding GPT-5.6 versions.

[3] GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna are rolling out gradually on Codex and ChatGPT Work, with token pricing lower than the previous-generation GPT-5.6. Sol is suited for handling complex coding and agentic workflows, while Luna is designed for tasks that require high focus and high throughput. The two models will be made available in phases to Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu users. Free and Go users can access Luna through the desktop app. Actual availability depends on the rollout progress and workspace settings; Enterprise administrators need to enable the new models themselves. Within ChatGPT, the two models are currently only available on Work and Codex and have not yet arrived on Chat.

[4] Worth noting: there is no so-called GPT-6 Terra. It appears OpenAI is phasing out mid-tier specifications and keeping only three tiers: Terra (small), Sol (large), and Astra (extra-large).

[5] Below is OpenAI's official announcement:

[6] Even though the most demanding and impactful work still requires Astra's full depth, different tasks have different scales, paces, and budgets. That is precisely why we are expanding the GPT-6 series with the launch of GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. GPT-6 Astra pioneered a new generation of intelligence, and these two new models further enhance cost-effectiveness, bringing these advantages to a broader range of users. We trained GPT-6 Sol and Luna using the same methodology used to train GPT-6 Astra, distilling Astra's leading capabilities in professional work, factual accuracy, coding, computer use, and model alignment into faster, more economical models.

[7] The company stated that both new models perform better than GPT-5.6 and are also priced lower than Astra (as well as the GPT-5.6 version it replaces). For example, the GPT-6 versions of Sol and Luna are priced 50% lower than their GPT-5.6 counterparts.
